To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a smart city is a city that is able to: 1) define a clear vision of what it wants to be and what it wants to achieve as a city, 2) define a clear strategy to become a smart, 3) define a clear set of objectives and KPI's to measure the progress of the smart city strategy, 4) organize a smart city program, 5) define a clear governance model for the program and 6) organize a smart community.
the smart city is not about technology, but about people.

smart city realization requires a city administration that: (1) has a clear vision and ambition for becoming a smart city, (2) has the right organization, (3) has a smart city strategy and plan, (4) is able to manage the complexity of the smart city project portfolio, (5) is able to create the right conditions for smart city projects to be successful and (6) has a smart governance approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how to turn smart city ambition into reality, and the answer is: by addressing the six challenges we identified.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the key to success for smart cities is to focus on the right things, in the right way, and at the right time.
a smart city is a city where the ambitions of its citizens are realized by an administration that has the capabilities to turn ambition into reality.

smart cities are a complex and multifaceted concept that requires a long-term vision, a holistic approach, an integrated and collaborative governance structure, an effective and efficient organizational setup, a strong and committed leadership and an open and flexible mindset.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ambition of becoming a smart and sustainable city is a very ambitious and complex endeavor, which is hard to manage, especially when it is a long-term endeavor.
smart city ambitions need to be turned into concrete actions, and that the city organization needs to be adapted to support those actions.
smart city realization is about more than just technology and data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ambition to be a smart cities is not only about the technology, it is also about a new way of thinking and working.
the ambition to become a smart and sustainable city is not a technical issue, but an organizational one.
the smart city is a process, rather than a state, and that a smart city needs to be managed as such.
